subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: A point P is moving on the curve y = 2x². The x-coordinate of P is increasing at the rate of 4 units/sec. Find the rate at which the y-coordinate is increasing when the point is at (2, 8).

mark_split.label: Differentiate y = 2x² with respect to t

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate y = 2x² with respect to t
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both x and y change with time, so the curve equation is differentiated with respect to t and not with respect to x. The chain rule line dy/dt = (dy/dx)(dx/dt) is what earns this mark.
lines: Given: dx/dt = 4 units/sec.  Asked: dy/dt at the point (2, 8).
P moves on the curve  y = 2x²
Differentiate both sides with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That y = 2x² is differentiated with respect to t, giving dy/dt = 4x(dx/dt) by the chain rule.
accept: differentiate the curve with respect to time using the chain rule
d y by d t equals d y by d x into d x by d t
the derivative of two x squared is four x
chain rule use chesi time tho differentiate cheyyali
d y by d t is four x into d x by d t
both coordinates change with time so differentiate with respect to t

steps.why: The point moves along the curve, so x and y are both functions of time. The chain rule is what carries the given rate dx/dt through the curve equation to the asked rate dy/dt.
common_mistakes: Stopping at dy/dx = 4x and giving 8 as the answer, which is a slope and not a rate.
Leaving out the dx/dt factor, which is where the given rate 4 enters.
steps.memory_tip: The chain rule reads left to right with dx cancelling: dy/dt = (dy/dx)(dx/dt). Write it in that order every time and the missing factor cannot be dropped.

steps.label: Substitute x = 2 and dx/dt = 4
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The point (2, 8) fixes x = 2; the y-value 8 is only a check that the point lies on the curve, since 2(2²) = 8. The unit units/sec is part of the answer.
lines: The point (2, 8) lies on the curve, since 2(2²) = 8, so x = 2 there.

recall.must_convey: That putting x = 2 and dx/dt = 4 into dy/dt = 4x(dx/dt) gives 32 units/sec.
accept: substitute x equal to two and d x by d t equal to four
four into two into four is thirty two
the y coordinate increases at thirty two units per second
x equal to two substitute cheste thirty two vasthundi
the answer is thirty two units per second
only the x value is needed from the point

steps.why: Only the x-coordinate of the point is needed, because dy/dt = 4x(dx/dt) contains x and no y. Checking that 2(2²) = 8 confirms the given point really is on the curve.
common_mistakes: Substituting y = 8 in place of x = 2.
Multiplying 4 × 2 and forgetting the second 4, giving 8.
steps.memory_tip: In dy/dt = 4x(dx/dt) there is no y, so from the point (2, 8) only the 2 is used and the 8 is just the check.

insider_note: Chain the rates: dy/dt = (dy/dx)(dx/dt). The point (2, 8) supplies x = 2, so dy/dx = 8 and the answer is 32.
